Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the retainage share, the contingency share, the overrun that is flagged, the selling costs and the profit you want from a flip.
List every work category of a project on Rehab lines with the budget, the contractor and the dates. Record the actual cost as the work is done; the variance and the budget flag fill in.

Write each property on Projects with its rehab budget, the planned end and the value after the work (ARV: the value once the work is finished). Spent, forecast cost, overrun, schedule and forecast profit fill in.
Ask for at least three bids for each category on Contractor bids and note the scope gap (the cost of what a bid leaves out). The true bid and the saving against the budget show which bid is best.

Record every draw on Draws: a draw is a payment released to a contractor as work is finished. The retainage held back and an inspection check fill in; Inspection records keep what the inspector found.
Write every change to the scope on Change orders before the work starts, with the reason and the amount. Approve only what fits the budget and the profit.
Track milestones, permits, material orders and the punch list on their own pages. Overdue and late rows turn red so a slip is visible early.
Use Holding costs and Contingency use to see what the project costs while it runs and how much of the reserve is gone.

Use the 14 calculators: budget builder, budget against actual, draw release, retainage, bid comparison, change order impact, flip profit, holding cost, schedule slip, maximum rehab, contingency, cost benchmark, value added and a grid.
Read the Renovation and Draws Dashboard and Charts every week: budget against actual, draws paid, change orders, overrun by project, holding cost, bids, milestones and the punch list.
Figures for tax, gains and sales are estimates: check with your own adviser, and check your own local rules for permits and safety, before you act on them.
Every unit, tenant, lease and late payment in one workbook
Rent roll, tenants, leases, arrears and vacancy for real estate investors
Rent roll with loss to lease and lease end alerts
every unit with its rent against the market rent, the days to the lease end and a flag when a renewal offer is still missing
Late rent and arrears tracker with payment plans
every month a tenant did not pay in full, with the plan, the last contact and the days open, so nothing is forgotten
days empty and listed rent become the rent lost, and the log shows which towns and quarters lose the most
the renewal rent, the market rent, the days empty and the turnover cost show which option earns more
the rent, the market rent and your limit become the new rent and the date the notice must go out
deposit, damage, cleaning and unpaid rent become the amount to return or the amount still owed
income, history, references and job stability become one score out of 100 and the same decision rule for every applicant
the move-in day and the monthly rent become the exact rent for the first part-month
rent due against rent collected for every month, with late and part payments split out
the clean, the paint, the repairs and the days empty become the full cost of re-letting a unit

Rent roll: every unit, tenant and lease
The list of units, tenants and rents; loss to lease (rent below the market rent), days to the lease end, the renewal flag, vacancy days and the rent owed fill in by themselves.
Rent payments: what was due and what was paid
One row for each unit and month with the rent due and the amount paid; days late, the balance, a payment check and the collection ratio fill in.
Arrears: rent owed and not paid, with payment plans
One row for each month a tenant did not pay in full, with the plan and the last contact; open or not, days open and the tenant phone fill in.
Leases: every lease with its term and rent
One row for each lease with the dates, the rent and the deposit; the property, the term in months, how long the tenant stayed and the days left fill in.
Renewals: lease end, offer and answer
One row for each lease end with the offer sent and the tenant answer; the increase percent, the days to the lease end and the contact phones fill in.
One row for each rent increase with the old and the new rent and whether the notice was sent; the increase percent, the send-by date and a cap check fill in.
Vacancy log: days empty and rent lost
One row for each time a unit sat empty with the date it emptied and the date it was filled; days vacant, the rent lost and a target check fill in.
Applicants: who asked for which unit
One row for each applicant with the income and the screening result; income as a multiple of the rent and an income check fill in.
Showings: who saw which unit and what happened
One row for each showing with the date and the outcome; the property, the rent asked and the applicant phone fill in.
Move-ins: condition and deposit at the start
One row for each move-in with the condition score and the deposit paid; the property and a condition check fill in.
One row for each move-out with the deposit, the deductions and the amount returned; the deduction share and a settlement check fill in.
Security deposits held for each unit
One row for each unit with the deposit held and since when; the property, the months of rent held and a status fill in. Check your own local rules for how deposits are held.
One row for each late fee with the month and the amount; whether it was collected, the share of the rent and the tenant fill in. Check your own local rules before you charge a fee.
Fee as a share of rent
Tenant requests: repairs asked for and how fast we answered
One row for each request from a tenant with the days to answer and the status; the tenant, the property, open or not and a speed check fill in.
Tenant contacts: phone and e-mail for each unit
One row for each unit with the tenant phone and e-mail; the property, the rent and the lease end fill in. Messages read the phone from here.
The market rent and the vacancy you expect for each town and number of bedrooms; the rent per bedroom and the gap to your own average rent fill in.
Properties: units and who manages them
The 16 properties with the type, the town and whether a manager runs them; the rent roll, the empty units and the open arrears fill in.
Unit inspections: score and issues found
One row for each inspection with the score and the issues found; the tenant, the property and a result check fill in.
